description: Portfolio has grown from 11 to 13 initiatives over recent heartbeats while completion rate remains under 10%. No initiative has ever been completed.

options.label: Moratorium on new initiatives

options.label: No moratorium

topic: Close desktop-monetization-assurance now that rollup is 2/2
description: desktop-monetization-assurance is marked active but both items (execute/lpbs-stripe-monetization-assurance-suite and research/lpbs-payment-guardrails-and-reconciliation-plan) are completed. It has no pending scope in Swarm Manager. Keeping it active misleads portfolio readouts by inflating 'active' count and can make the dashboard treat it as if work remains. Any net-new monetization assurance work already exists in the backlog as independent items (lpbs-payment-anomaly-log-and-alerts, lpbs-checkout-webhook-atomicity, lpbs-upsert-asset-hardcoded-variant-key) and could either stay standalone or be rolled under desktop-release-governance.

options.label: Close initiative
options.rationale: Flip status to completed. Matches current 2/2 rollup. Net-new follow-on work stays standalone or folds into desktop-release-governance.

options.label: Keep active and expand scope
options.rationale: Attach follow-on items (lpbs-payment-anomaly-log-and-alerts, lpbs-checkout-webhook-atomicity, lpbs-upsert-asset-hardcoded-variant-key) so the initiative remains a coherent monetization-assurance umbrella.

options.label: Leave as-is
options.rationale: Accept the status drift; document manually.

notes: Operator wants to keep initiative open for upcoming swarm-manager initiative-level review/follow-up features; plans to perform a review on this one specifically. Decision closed without mutating initiative status. If review surfaces follow-ups, option B (expand scope) becomes the right call at that point.

topic: Resolve initiative edge drift surfaced by swarm-manager overview
description: swarm-manager overview consistency reports 2 missing_explicit edges (child items cross an initiative boundary with no declared parent-initiative dependency) and ~12 possibly_stale edges (declared initiative dependency has no supporting child dependency). Hygiene, not blockers, but unresolved drift erodes trust in the sequencing signal portfolio-manager relies on. Missing_explicit: (1) contribution-outbound-v1-bug-reports -> contribution-settings via execute/contribution-submitter-bug-report, (2) desktop-runtime-interop -> emulator-platform via execute/desktop-ecosystem-interop-regression-coverage. Possibly_stale set spans agent-inbox-unified-retrieval, agent-sandbox-audit-foundation, contribution-inbound-triage, contribution-outbound-extensions, contribution-verification-isolated, decision-visual-grounding-propagation, desktop-release-governance, director-dashboard-gap-workflow, ecosystem-intelligence-loop, and others.

options.label: Add the two missing_explicit edges; keep possibly_stale as-is
options.rationale: Missing edges are real dependencies the graph is hiding. Possibly_stale often reflects architectural (not item-level) dependencies that are legitimately declared only at the initiative level. Minimum-churn fix.

options.label: Add missing + drop all possibly_stale
options.rationale: Treat the graph as strictly item-derived. Aggressive cleanup; risks losing coarse-grained architectural dependencies that never had matching item edges.

options.label: Defer all edge cleanup
options.rationale: Accept drift; revisit when initiative-level dependency mutation tooling lands.

notes: Add the two missing_explicit edges; leave possibly_stale alone. Operator also endorsed a systemic follow-up: run the consistency check on every mutation that could affect edges (item create/edit/move/delete, initiative edit), surface drift delta on API/CLI/UI response with a suggested one-step fix, and add a vetted mark for legitimately architectural possibly_stale edges so they stop being repeat noise. Captured for backlog in Phase 8.

rationale: Directly addresses the candidate future proposal carried forward from the previous portfolio-manager handoff, now that both previously pending portfolio decisions have resolved. Keeps approval debt low (one net-new pending decision) and anchors against PORTFOLIO_PHILOSOPHY criterion 1 (revenue) via monetization CATALOG.md.
topic: Stand up web-console-readiness initiative for the business-bundle co-headliner
description: web-console is the business bundle's second headliner per docs/monetization/catalog/base/business.md. GCT has six dedicated initiatives (ai-provenance, commit-initiative-linking, github-integration, pre-commit-security, merge-and-conflicts, release-pipeline). web-console has none. web-console-specific hardening items currently live under 'continuous-audio-platform' (fix/web-console-vad-false-silence, fix/web-console-tts-summarization-bug, execute/web-console-audio-test-hardening, execute/web-console-adopt-audio-tools), which is description-ally about audio extraction into a shared audio-tools scenario, not about web-console's paid-release readiness. Standalone items (execute/web-console-tts-code-tick-handling, idea/web-console-archived) also spill around the backlog. Portfolio effect: without a dedicated initiative, there is no single surface that tracks whether the bundle's co-headliner is actually approaching paid-release readiness. Theme mapping is clear (Theme 2 — Bundle Scenarios). This is an initiative-shape proposal (multiple dependent items under one outcome), not a single backlog item.

options.label: Create web-console-readiness initiative (Theme 2) scoped to paid-release readiness of the web-console headliner
options.rationale: At workshop time, move the web-console-specific items currently under continuous-audio-platform (fix/web-console-vad-false-silence, fix/web-console-tts-summarization-bug, execute/web-console-audio-test-hardening, execute/web-console-adopt-audio-tools) plus standalone items (execute/web-console-tts-code-tick-handling) under it. Leave audio-tools-greenfield-scenario and the adoption items for swarm-manager/agent-manager under continuous-audio-platform since those are about the shared audio scenario, not web-console itself.

options.label: Keep status quo
options.rationale: Web-console items stay under continuous-audio-platform and scattered backlog. Accept the portfolio-readout limitation that the bundle co-headliner has no dedicated tracking surface.

options.label: Defer until the first GCT-headliner paid release closes
options.rationale: Web-console readiness becomes the next initiative only after GCT ships paid, on the theory that shipping one headliner matters more than parallel readiness work.

notes: Accepted 2026-04-24 vision walk (resumed from 2026-04-23 deferral). Deferral condition met: coverage-visibility plan (docs/plans/portfolio-manager-scenario-coverage-implementation-plan.md) shipped 2026-04-24 11:46 EDT. Operator designated web-console-readiness as the highest-priority action of this walk. At workshop time: relocate fix/web-console-vad-false-silence, fix/web-console-tts-summarization-bug, execute/web-console-audio-test-hardening, execute/web-console-adopt-audio-tools, execute/web-console-tts-code-tick-handling under the new initiative; leave audio-tools-greenfield-scenario items under continuous-audio-platform.

topic: Tier-3 (hosted-cloud) positioning vs web-console headliner status
description: The 2026-04-25 vision walk surfaced a question: should web-console-readiness depend on a hosted-Vrooli cloud-tier prerequisite, since web-console's most compelling pitch (use it from your phone) requires Vrooli to run somewhere the customer can reach without self-hosting? Investigation confirmed docs/monetization/catalog/base/business.md positions web-console as already-deployable for self-hosters with a real but narrow audience. The decision is whether to (A) hard-reorder headliners and gate web-console-readiness on a Tier 3 prerequisite, (B) skip Tier 3 work entirely and keep self-host as the only path, or (C) keep web-console's headliner status accurate for self-hosters while adding Tier 3 as a parallel expansion that opens the larger phone-anywhere market.

options.label: Hard reorder — GCT becomes #1, web-console-readiness depends_on hosted-cloud-tier-foundation, catalog repositioned
options.rationale: Phone-anywhere is the load-bearing pitch; without it web-console is just a fancier terminal. Forces sequencing discipline.

options.label: No Tier 3 work — keep catalog as-is; phone-anywhere remains permanently aspirational
options.rationale: Self-host audience is enough; saves operational complexity of running customer instances.

options.label: Coexistence — keep catalog headliner status; create hosted-cloud-tier-foundation as Tier 3 expansion; no depends_on edge
options.rationale: Catalog framing is accurate for self-hosters; Tier 3 expands addressable market without invalidating Tier 1 pitch. Both audiences get served. Filed alongside this decision: initiative hosted-cloud-tier-foundation (priority 6, status active, foundation pattern).

notes: Operator selected coexistence at the moment of filing. Initiative hosted-cloud-tier-foundation is already active (priority 6, created same day). Web-console-readiness is unchanged — no depends_on edge, no catalog repositioning. Both pitches operate in parallel: Tier 1 self-host pitch as currently catalogued, Tier 3 hosted pitch as the new expansion path. Future telemetry on Tier 1 audience size may revisit this; not encoded today. See orchestration-summary.md on hosted-cloud-tier-foundation for the full reasoning chain.
